cells.king: Vīra-Narasimharāya, “ruling from his jewelled throne at Vijayapura.”
cells.remarks: Registers the conferment of the right of worship and management in the temple of Sthalasayana-Perumāḷ at Kuḍalamai on Pijjalōkāchārya, son of Śathagōpāchārya, of the Gōtama-gōtra and Āpastamba-sūtra by Rāmachandrarāja, alias Parāṅkuśadāsa, son of Raghunāthārāja and grandson of Rāmabhadrarāja, who was the agent of Aḷiyārāmarāja and Iśvara kuṃmīddhāna. Parāṅkuśadāsa is also said to have effected some repairs in the temple and revived an old festival therein.

cells.remarks: Registers a sale of land by the assembly of the village Rāja-chandra-chaturvēdimangalam, to Vīra-Paṭṭāḷakan alias Paramāṇanda Śarkaraiyār of Kumāramangalam in Ārūr-kūṟṟam, a subdivision of Śōḻanāḍu, who placed it in the temple of the god in the same village, for conducting the Śrībali ceremony in the temple of the god at Kāyambāḍu. cells.location: Kaḍambūr
cells.place: On the south wall of the deserted Śiva temple.
cells.remarks: Ends of lines lost. Seems to register a gift of land as dēvadāna at Kaḍambūr in Nandipura-śīrmai was in his nāya-kaṭṭaṇam, and of the village Puḍukkulam, by a brother (name lost) of Vīra-Śaḷa-Nāya-Nāyaka, for the merit of Kōṇḍama-Nāyaka of Kaḍambūr, to meet the expenses of worship and repairs therein. Records also a subsequent gift, for the same purpose, of the village Nāṭṭēri in the month of Aippāśi in the year Viṣhu, for the merit of Aṅgappa-Nāya-Nāyaka, of Koṇḍama-Nāyaka and Tippu-Nāyaka, sons of Nīlagaṇṭha-Nāyaka, for the welfare of their family (gōtra).

cells.remarks: States that the sluice, evidently of the tank at Kāvērippākkam, was repaired by Śeṅgēṇi-Mirdan Śiyaṅ Virāśāni Ammaiappan Kaṇṇuḍai-Perumāḷ alias Vīraviṇōdan Vīra-māḍa Śāmbuvarāyan and called Vīraviṇōdan-tumbu after him. Two other fragments are recorded of the 3rd and 6th years of the same king are also engraved on this slab.

cells.date: Śaka 1450, Sarvadhārin, Mēsha, śu. 5, Thursday, Puśam.
cells.remarks: Records the gift, under some stipulation, of house-sites and lands and the right of uḷavu-kāṇi on kuḍiningādēva-dāna lands at Teḷḷār, to the temple-staff, by Kupam-Bhaṭṭan, Āḷampirān-Bhaṭṭan, son of Iḷaiyaperumāḷ, a brāhmaṇa of the Kauśika-gōtra at Kiliyānagar, who had constructed a car for the god Tirumulathānam-Uḍaiyār at Teḷḷār, and who had populated a village under the name Kiliyānagar-agaram and built a tank for it. He was given the right of handling the cash and ornaments of the temple. Records also another gift of some lands and house-sites in the village....paṭṭa, which had been granted to the temple by Tirumala-Nāyaka for the merit of Immaḍi-Rāyappa-Nāyaka.

cells.date: Chāḷukya-Vikrama year 7, Rākshasa, Uttarāyaṇa-saṅkrānti, śu. 1, Monday. [date-calculation appendix, No. 47: Chālukya-Vikrama year 7, Raktākshi, Uttarāyaṇa-saṅkrānti, Vyatīpāta, ēkādaśī, Monday. Raktākshi in the king’s reign corresponded to A.D. 1144-45, and so Chālukya-Vikrama year 7 is a mistake for 67. The details agree for A.D. 1144, December 25, Monday. Uttarāyaṇa-saṅkrānti occurred on the previous day and the tithi was Pushya ba. 14. Ēkādaśī quoted in the record is evidently a mistake.]

Also registers minor gifts of money made to some artisans to the same temple.

cells.remarks: Records a gift of taxes made by Daṇḍanāyaka Sōmēśvara- Bhaṭṭa to Dāsa-Gāvuṇḍa of Ukkuṇḍa included in Saṭṭa- lige-70. Also registers another gift of taxes made by Śivāyitadēva and donee while Mahāmaṇḍaḷēś- vara Vijayādityadēva of the Maṇḍali-12,000 provinces, lord of Beḷhuṇḍe-70, Muguṇḍa-12, Eḍenāḍu-70, Uḍuru- 12, Ējūru and Kaivatti and of the manneya of Kaṇṇavaḷḷi and Mahāpradhāna Sōmēśvaradēva was the ruler of the Two Six-hundred and Banavāsi-12,000 provinces. States that Dāsa-Gāvuṇḍa constructed a tank and granted land to Abhimānasiṅgha-Paṇḍita, a disciple of Gaṅgāśiva- Paṇḍita.
